summary.text: 家 combines 宀, associated with a roof or dwelling, with the lower form 豕. The lower element’s earliest identity and role are disputed: it has been interpreted as a pig in a meaningful scene or, in the traditional account, as an abbreviated phonetic form of 豭. Early dwelling and household uses are reported; the character commonly means house, home, or family today.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. The traditional analysis treats 宀 as a dwelling element and proposes the lower form as an abbreviation of 豭 used for sound, but the evidence here does not establish 豭 as a graphic ancestor or positional full form of 豕. Other interpretations take the lower element as a pig depicted beneath a roof, sometimes proposing an original meaning ‘pig enclosure’; that proposed origin is not established.

components.text: 宀 contributes the roof or dwelling idea. It is present as a full component; no distinct earlier form is proposed.

The visible lower component is 豕. The traditional analysis proposes 豭 as its abbreviated phonetic counterpart, but does not establish 豭 as 豕’s graphic ancestor or full form. Other accounts interpret the element as a pig in the scene. The proposed earlier sign 𢑓 and its alleged change into 豕 remain unverified.

sound_limitation.text: The readings and reconstructions support sound compatibility if 豭 is the relevant element, but do not establish the earliest lower sign’s identity or provide a reading for proposed sign 𢑓.

sound.text: Modern Mandarin readings match. This comparison supports compatibility only if 豭 is the relevant element; it does not assign a reading to visible 豕.
The Baxter–Sagart reconstruction gives 豭 and 家 the same Middle Chinese form, kae, supporting phonetic compatibility if 豭 is the relevant element.
The Baxter–Sagart reconstruction gives 豭 and 家 the same Old Chinese form, *kˤra, supporting phonetic compatibility if 豭 is the relevant element.

history.text: The traditional written analysis identifies the lower form as an abbreviation of 豭 used for sound; the regular-script character writes 豕 beneath 宀. This records the traditional analysis and familiar form, not proof of the earliest construction or a graphic derivation of 豕 from 豭.
A claim that oracle-bone 𢑓 was the original lower sign and later changed into 豕 through graphic corruption has not been verified from primary paleographic evidence.

uncertainties.text: The earliest identity and role of the lower element remain unsettled. Some analyses connect it with 豭 as a sound element; others see a pig contributing to a meaningful scene and propose a pig enclosure as the origin. That proposed origin is not established.
Matching readings and reconstructions for 豭 and 家 do not prove that the earliest lower sign was named 豭. No independent ancient pronunciation for a proposed depicted animal or sign is established.

senses.period: Oracle-bone uses are reported; dates of individual examples are unresolved
senses.text: Early uses associated with dwelling are reported, including human dwelling in oracle-bone contexts. A pig-enclosure meaning has been proposed as an origin, but is not established as the earliest meaning.

senses.gloss: ancestral temple, family, royal house or household unit
senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze uses are reported; sequence unresolved
senses.text: Reported uses include ancestral temple and family, royal house or court, and households counted as 家. Their order and relationships are not established.
家 commonly means house or home, and also family. How these current meanings connect to each reported early institutional use is not established.

developments.text: Dwelling and household or institutional uses are both reported early, but their sequence and any development from one to the other are not established.
Modern house, home, and family meanings are established, but the chronology and transitions linking them to early reported uses remain unclear.

limitations.text: The reported early uses do not provide a dated sequence of examined inscriptions. Individual examples and the chronology of meanings remain unresolved.

The pig-enclosure proposal connects a proposed early meaning to human dwelling; the traditional phonetic analysis instead explains the graph through sound. Neither account establishes a full chronology of the word’s meanings.

overview.text: 家 combines a roof or dwelling element with a lower form whose identity and role are disputed. Early dwelling and household uses are reported; today it commonly means house, home, or family.

components.text: 宀 contributes the roof or dwelling idea in the proposed construction.
The lower form is 豕. It may depict a pig or stand for 豭 as a sound element; that proposed sound analysis does not establish the lower sign’s graphic history.

relationships.text: In the proposed construction, 宀 contributes the roof or dwelling category.
Some accounts interpret the lower element as a pig contributing to a scene of livestock kept beneath a roof.

The traditional analysis proposes that the visible lower form represents an abbreviated 豭 used for sound. Matching readings and reconstructions make this plausible, but do not settle the earliest sign’s identity or establish a graphic derivation.
